chapter: Uptown versus downtown styles and Tom Anderson's
title: Ragtime versus Dixieland, uptown versus downtown, and the blues
summary: Downtown bands read music and played waltzes and quadrilles; uptown played blues by ear.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: they gave them different names, ragtime, this kind, that kind. But they all played a similar style of music, whether they call themselves a different style of band or not. You say that the ragtime band played different, for instance, than the Dixieland band?
Well, just the ones that, just like, first say, from uptown, they would call themselves the ragtime bands. And the ones from downtown called Dixieland, you see, most of them.
Is there any difference much in the style of music uptown and downtown?

No, not much. They all practiced, played about the most of the same style of music. The ones downtown they really played, they had to play a lot of waltzes and a lot of mazookas and pokas and quadrilles and things like that, you see. And that style of music was at that time. And the ones uptown that it was most they played was the blues. They played a lot of blues.
They played them similar to what they play them nowadays?

Yeah, they're the same old blues. That's one blues the same. But they've made little changes to it, you see. These writers now, they've taken the original blues and just making changes with them, you see. But the old time blues, they didn't have no more than about three or four changes in the blues. The old time blues. The same thing over and over all the time.
Well, it was mostly the fellas downtown, all them days there, they played more of music. Oh yeah. They fellas uptown, they played more of air. Air, air, you see. And that was a different one.
In other words, it's like saying.
As far as downtown you could play, you could play the red books.

Yeah, all they had, they could, the ones from downtown, they really were strictly musicians, you see. Yeah, they studied more of music. They were what they call educated musicians. The fellas from uptown there, they were like a talent fellas, you see. They could play anything they hear, you see.

They didn't need no music. They all followed suit. They all played one player, same tune, and the other played the same tune. And they made a little more. They was playing night and day. Yeah. They was dancing. I was telling them Sunday, all since you're old, they knew all that.
Dance, man. Every night, playing the houses, the Tanya Street, all in the big white people.
